newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico building industry sees better times in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico building industry sees better times in 1997.

text.p: Mexico's hard-hit construction industry could resume in 1997 the growth it had enjoyed prior to the December 1994 devaluation, an industry leader told Reuters on Thursday.

"1994 growth rates are within our reach," said Fernando Acosta, president of the National Construction Industry Chamber (CNIC). Acosta said he foresaw growth in all areas, including housing, urban development and infrastructure.
Growth in the Mexican construction industry slumped by almost 30 percent in 1995, after being one of the more vigorous sectors of the economy in 1993 and 1994.

Acosta said the industry planned to build more than the official construction target of 250,000 units specified in the Alliance for Economic Growth (ACE). The ACE, signed last Saturday, is an agreement between government, business and labor leaders on a package of economic measures.
"We plan an extra 75,000 units for next year, and with 325,000 units in total, the housing sector will be fully recovered," Acosta said.

"Our housing program varies between 70,000 and 90,000 pesos per unit. The private sector will cover 50 percent of the financing, the government 40 percent and the buyer the remaining 10 percent," he said.
"For infrastructure projects, we are thinking of drawing foreign investment with a domestic share. We have 142 urban developments agreed with the government," he added.
-- Mara Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9553
